📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

In a recent development, when it comes to stylish couples, Rihanna and A$AP Rocky are a match made in fashion heaven. Ever since their relationship turned romantic over five years ago, the pair have made it seem like they’ve been pulling from a his-and-hers closet. From their dramatic plush coats at the Met Gala to their matching olive moment on the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever red carpet, their coordinating looks are always on point. But, even more impressively, they always manage to complement one other without losing their individual sense of style.

On Monday afternoon, that impressive display continued as the stars were seen in Beverly Hills, California, where the dress code of the day appeared to be “open jackets and substantial pants.” It was the first time in weeks that the pair has been seen in public together, as A$AP has been on his Don’t Be Dumb Tour across Europe for the past couple of months.

For the outing, Rihanna curated a watermelon color scheme up top, layering a soft pink T-shirt underneath an army-green parka, presumably from Celine.

The utility-style outerwear featured rows of pockets in front and a plush brown shearling collar that also lined the inside of the jacket and cuffs. Notably, Rihanna may have borrowed the coat from her stylist, Jahleel Weaver, as he posted an Instagram Story yesterday afternoon in which he was seen wearing the exact same one.

It has been revealed that to complete her fit, the “Diamonds” singer wore baggy white jeans and a pair of strappy white stilettos. Oh, and our queen of statement glasses added a set of cranberry-colored visor shades.

For his part, Rocky stacked a dark-wash jean jacket and a creamy corduroy one over a black tee, completing the fit with obsidian wide-leg slacks and inky leather Oxfords. As for his sunglasses, the Ray-Ban creative director chose a pair of the brand’s classic aviators.

The couple’s outing comes days after their daughter, Rocki, made her high-fashion debut in a new Dior campaign, proving that every member of this family really is programmed to have incredible style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re looking hard enough for sales on menswear, you can almost always find a discount on something decent, a pair of shoes, a shirt maybe, but you have to scrounge. Every other week of the year, that’s just how it is. But this week, the week of Black Friday, the opposite is true. Every store and their mother is having a sale and suddenly, it’s not easy to tell which markdowns are gonna go fast and which ones will still be there when you log on again in December. Luckily, you have me. Year-round, it’s my job to keep tabs on deals so I know which ones to pounce on this Black Friday.

On Amazon, there’s my favorite Lacoste polo, which is actually on an outrageous sale going up to 40 percent off if you’re the right size. Filson jackets are 25 percent off. Lululemon isn’t just for the gals, it has a ton of great stuff for men and its Black Friday sale is absolutely stacked. And REI is doing its classic “We hate Black Friday but are doing a sale anyway” thing, and as always we are here for it.

Let’s start with the personal favorites; after that we’ll just list deals alphabetically by brand. First, Amazon. Yeah, yeah, everything is Amazon now. But when Bezos is offering massive discounts on Lacoste polos and Levi’s, we listen.

It has been revealed that nothing is ever going to beat the cool of a beat-to-hell Filson jacket. If you’ve been holding off on buying one, I can’t recommend it enough. Plus, Black Friday is the perfect time to get one for 25 percent off.

FIlson Tin Cloth Insulated Jacket.

According to recent reports, I tell regular—meaning normal guys, not fashion-y dorks like me—that Huckberry is really the answer to 90 percent of what they want. All of a man’s casual wardrobe can be bought here; the only thing it doesn’t stock well is suits and tailoring. I’m seeing up to 40 percent off on seasonal shirts, and up to 30 percent off jackets, sweaters, and pants; that’s as good as it gets, folks.

Proof 72-Hour Merino 5-Pocket Pant.

Flint and Tinder Bolinas Johnny Collar Sweater Polo.

Flint and Tinder Boiled Wool Chore Blazer.

There’s nowhere better for well-made classics of American menswear. It’s one of the brands I come back to time and time again for sweaters, shirts, anything really. This holiday, J. Press has 40 percent off elevated basics that will last.

Sources indicate that J. Press “Ivy Guy” Blue Striped Oxford Cloth Sport Shirt.

J. Press Made-in-England Khaki Drywax Cotton Overshirt.

Sources indicate that J. Press Blue Wool Crewneck Sweater.

Industry observers note that any time Lululemon does a discount is noteworthy. The brand is averse to any seasonal sales, so Black Friday is your best bet here. Through Cyber Monday, you can get substantial discounts (I’m talking 40-plus percent off) on the usual best sellers—just note that for the most part, only certain colors are discounted.

Lululemon Smooth Spacer Classic-Fit Pullover Hoodie.

Lululemon Pace Breaker Linerless Shorts.

Lululemon Navigation Down Hoodie.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re not a regular Huckberry guy but a man who considers himself “into fashion” or at least “stylish,” you ought to be hitting the Mr Porter sale. The sale is absolutely massive—over 12,000 items are up to 50 percent off—so I’d go in with a strategy. Have one item, or even one brand, you want to check out; do that and that only. My hunt is for a really good jacket—sport coat, blazer, suit separate, or whatever you want to call it. That’s what I’m showing, but you need to do some of your own hunting on this one.

Brunello Cucinelli Shearling-Trimmed Suede Trucker Jacket.

Maison Margiela Replica Suede-Trimmed Leather Sneakers.

All right, the rest of these I’m presenting brand by brand in alphabetical order. I’ll spare you a spiel on each one, but if you need some guidance, let me call out a few heavy hitters.

Del Toro, which has for a long time just been a really good rich guy made-in-Italy shoe brand, has started putting out some really lovely elevated casual clothing—all vintage Italian-inspired stuff—and a majority of it is 20 percent off. And J. Crew has its usual sale going on, but an extra 40 percent off sale styles thrown in with the code FRIDAY on top of that. Todd Snyder is giving 30 percent off a ton of items with the code BLACKFRIDAY. And of course, you can’t go wrong at perennial favorite outlets REI and Nordstrom—both are featuring affordable menswear at a discount for Black Friday.

10 Sheer, Minimalist Winter Nail Ideas, From Lavender Cream to Soft Stardust

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (525 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The allure of soft, understated nails is going nowhere.
  • Recent findings suggest that for winter, this translates to sheer, milky tones, short, considered nail shapes and microvariations of wearable nail art.
  • Essie Gel Couture Long-Lasting Nail Polish in Liquid Diamonds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The allure of soft, understated nails is going nowhere. Rather, throughout 2026, we’ve seen the minimalist manicure movement gain momentum with each newly introduced season. “It’s the biggest shift I’ve seen in my chair this year,” indicates celebrity nail technician Iram Shelton. She explains that the theme has been “natural nails, but better,” which is centered around low-maintenance colors and finishes.

Recent findings suggest that for winter, this translates to sheer, milky tones, short, considered nail shapes and microvariations of wearable nail art. In preparation for party season, expect to see minuscule flecks of metallic gold and star-themed motifs, too. While milky pink nails will always be in style, this winter, it’s all about unexpected sheers like lavender, bronze, and pearly white. Not only do these colors go with everything, but they also are extremely forgiving—you can paint them on yourself without a problem.

Zoya Lavender Perfector Nail Polish.

Londontown Illuminating Nail Concealer in Bare.

Essie Gel Couture Long-Lasting Nail Polish in Liquid Diamonds.

Below, find 10 of the most polished, pared-back nail ideas to bookmark for your next appointment.

Last season, we had Hailey Bieber milk nails, followed by Sienna Miller’s ‘Chantilly cream’. Now? Lavender takes the spotlight, in its dreamiest, near-translucent form. A high-shine top coat makes this tone appear even hazier in the light.

In a recent development, leaning into minimalism doesn’t necessarily mean forgoing color. Take this rich, berry red for proof; when an all-over pigment isn’t on the cards, a sleek micro French tip is equally flattering.

Recent findings suggest that for a simpler take on autumn’s ‘gold fairy dust’ nail trend (as seen on Taylor Swift), draw inspiration from stardust instead. Here, a natural blushed pink base sits beautifully under a gently dazzling, golden shimmer top coat.

Sources indicate that traditional French tips are given a modern, metallic upgrade without veering into futuristic territory. When reserved for the base of the nail, a gold-toned cuff is eye-catching but in a subtle way.

Sources indicate that frosted pearlescent finishes are as luminous as they are delicate—not to mention destined for winter weather. When worn with a cozy cashmere knit, you’d be hard-pressed to find a more perfect pairing.

It has been revealed that square and squoval nails are seeing a revival this season. Keep your shapes cropped, softly rounded, and ultra-glossy if committing to minimalism.

Trade in winter's deep, vibrant mocha, espresso, and cocoa-inspired browns for a sheer bronze pigment. When kept close to the natural nail color, this shade is the best way to embrace elevated color without going overboard.

While the notion of nail art might suggest something elaborate colorful, petite star motifs make a case for the opposite. One on each nail balances a feeling of festivity with practicality for everyday wear.

In a recent development, granted, a white Christmas might be far on the horizon. But this set sees micro polka dots get a dainty, wintry upgrade, inspired by tiny droplets of snow.

If a micro French isn’t your style, an ombré is worth considering. Begin with a nude beige-pink base color, and watch it blend seamlessly into a cozy, seasonal color.

According to recent reports, we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

If there's one outerwear trend I can't stop noticing this season, it's faux fur. And Kylie Jenner's fashion brand KHY has certainly caught my attention. I can’t scroll on TikTok without someone mentioning how nice Jenner’s coat selection is. And given that they’re always sold out, I wanted to see what the hype was all about. KHY released in 2023, and while the brand has been releasing interesting pieces, their regular clothing hasn’t always grabbed my attention. But these coats seem to be the rising notable staple fashion people are wanting to buy.

Sources indicate that online shopping isn’t always the easiest, especially when it comes to coats. So, for my Los Angeles fashion lovers, you can experience KHY a little more close-up in the coming weeks. KHY will be opening up the I <3 LA POP-UP, its first space of its own, on Sunset Boulevard in West Hollywood. The limited-time pop-up will be open from Friday, December 4 through Sunday, December 13, and will feature an assortment of KHY's best sellers and exclusive pieces, including the KHY After Dark coats—which are the pieces I was able to snag for this review that are currently sold out on the website.

Industry observers note that because there is a ton of interest, I tried two of KHY's faux-fur coats for myself, photographing each to see how they look away from the perfectly styled campaign images. From the fit and feel to the overall finish, here's my honest verdict on whether Kylie Jenner's faux-fur coats deserve a place in your winter wardrobe.

This coat immediately caught my attention while on the KHY site. I love a dramatic moment and this fits the bill. I got the most compliments while wearing this black faux-fur coat and it makes sense because it’s the epitome of opulence. I’m wearing a 3X and I will say it’s a bit snug. I normally wear a 16/18 U.S. women’s, so that would translate to a 1X or 2X depending on the brand, so definitely sizing up would be ideal if you want a bit more room in your fit. The arm length was great and I dealt with minimal shedding.

Funny enough, I didn’t love this coat when I first pulled it out of the package, but my coworker and I laughed at how once I put it on it was actually so much cuter. This was also a fan favorite from one of my friends, as he said it seems “more versatile” than the dramatic all-black one. So if you’re looking for an everyday faux-fur coat, this one is definitely top of mind. This was also a 3X and it actually fit much looser than the Marmont Sculpted Coat, but the fur trim did interfere with the zipper that’s tucked beneath the chest area. So, if you’re a fuller-chest girl like myself, still sizing up would be your best route.

In a recent development, while the After Dark Collection is currently sold out, there likely will be a restock because of how popular the coats are. Until then, here are a few other KHY selects and faux-fur favorites I’ve been eyeing that you can shop right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when you're wrapping up Thanksgiving dinner, you're probably looking for a tasty drink and a little something sweet to finish the meal. But why not have both at the same time with a dessert cocktail? This boozy Turkeytini has all you need to complete your Thanksgiving feast with the decadent blend of creamy Baileys Irish cream, chocolate liqueur, Kahlúa, and bourbon.

Hot tip: Make sure to shake the cocktail for a good 20 seconds or more to get it homogeneous and frothy. This is the secret to getting a smooth drink without any curdling or separation. This recipe makes one drink, but feel free to increase all the ingredients to make a massive batch—plus, the more Reese's, the better!

According to recent reports, the garnish:It's entirely optional, but I took a note from our Oreo turkeys and made an adorable Reese's turkey as a garnish for this drink. Here's how you do it: Dot the back of 2 candy eyes with melted chocolate. Place on a Reese’s Thins cup. Use more chocolate to attach the orange part of a candy corn as the beak. For feathers, halve another cup and attach to the back with more chocolate. I promise it will make your drink all the more delicious (and adorable).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chicago is a great place to be year-round (yes, even in the dead of winter). And it doesn’t hurt that there’s always plenty to see and do. Spend the day at the Art Institute of Chicago, grab a deep-dish pizza at Pequod’s, or simply explore the city and see where the day takes you. If you’re planning to be in town this weekend or over the holidays, Chi-town is ripe for a visit—or even a staycation. Whether you’re heading to the Windy City for the art, the food, or a future music festival, consider this your nonexhaustive guide to what to see, where to eat, and everything in between.

In a recent development, known for its sprawling campus and sun-soaked galleries filled with modernist and contemporary masterpieces, the Art Institute of Chicago in Grant Park remains one of the oldest and largest art museums in the world, dating all the way back to 1879. The permanent collections are exceptional, but the Institute’s heavy rotation of standout exhibitions makes it worth the visit.

According to recent reports, no visit to Chicago is complete without enjoying some jazz. Situated in Chicago’s Uptown neighborhood, the iconic century-old Green Mill plays host to live music seven days a week, with Thursday nights specifically dedicated to swing dancing and the third Sunday of every month to poetry slams. This famed, cash-only entertainment venue was a local haunt of mobster Al Capone, who frequented the establishment during Prohibition. Patrons can still sit in his booth, which has a clear view of both exits (for obvious reasons).

Sources indicate that get lost among the Spanish Baroque-style structures capped with gold rotundas, lagoons, and more, before arriving at the stunning glass greenhouse that ensconces the Garfield Park Conservatory. Traverse through the manicured gardens and wander between themed rooms with spaces dedicated to palms, ferns, desert cacti, succulents, and exotic flora (why not?). Throughout the year, the Conservatory hosts special pop-up events like beer tastings, yoga, expert talks, and, yes, flower highlights.

Guest In Residence Grizzly Jacket.

In a recent development, top Chef winner and South Side native Joe Flamm brings Italian-Croatian flavor to the West Loop’s Fulton Market district with his restaurant Rose Mary. The buzzy concept offers a modern take on rustic dishes, packed with bold flavors and thoughtful coursing that encapsulates what Flamm has coined “Adriatic drinking food.” The open kitchen gives dining patrons a glimpse of all the action, and amid exacting sous chefs, you’ll sometimes see chef Joe himself calling the shots. While the menu changes seasonally, the Stracciatella starter is a must, and you can’t go wrong with the Mafaldine or Pork Ribs Pampanella.

According to recent reports, lincoln Park’s crown jewel, Alinea, is renowned for its ingenious molecular gastronomy, led by creative chef Grant Achatz, who has earned the eatery three Michelin stars and a bevy of awards. Enter through an unmarked door and enjoy a multi-course tasting menu with inventive creations like a single-bite black truffle explosion or a complex take on surf and turf with nuanced flavors plated with surgical precision, and a dessert finale that looks like a literal splatter of paint right on your dining table. The Alinea experience comes complete with scented vapors, tricks, and tableside theatrics, so you’ll be plenty entertained throughout.

If you want the ultimate deep-dish experience, Pequod’s reigns supreme. It’s been an institution since the ’70s and an undisputed choice among locals for traditional pan pizza (hold for those who will try to keep this a secret from out-of-towners). What sets Pequod’s apart from other deep-dish joints is the crunchy, caramelized crust that some will say is a transcendent experience, making it the best pizza in Chicago, if not one of the best in the country.

It has been revealed that where better to enjoy a martini than under 24-karat gold Tiffany & Co. candelabras and Grecian frescos by French painter Louis Pierre Rigal? Palmer House is opulence defined—a hotel packed with history and enduring romantic myths that swirl around its origins. Enter the lobby through the travertine double staircase and you’re immediately transported to another universe. The French-inspired aesthetic can trace its roots back to Bertha Palmer, the lucky dame who was gifted the hotel as an extravagant wedding gift by her husband, Potter Palmer. After befriending Claude Monet, she began amassing a remarkable amount of Impressionist art that stood as the largest collection outside of France (now on display at the Art Institute). Enjoy a cocktail at Palmer’s Lockwood Lobby Bar before starting your evening. Pro tip: Live entertainment is offered on weekends.

Tucked away in a secret alleyway entrance, Three Dots and a Dash is a whimsical take on an island bar, with exotic craft cocktails and tropical elixirs. Pick your poison by flavor, clever name, or the eccentric mug it’s housed in. For rum connoisseurs, the Bamboo Room inside offers a dedicated experience with a focused menu of daiquiris, renditions of classics, and progressive cocktails made using a modern technique.

This sprawling rooftop at the edge of Navy Pier has the best perch in town, with sweeping views of Lake Michigan and the coastal skyline. The bright and airy space is open year-round, with fire pits, game areas, and cozy seating ideal for group hangs and intimate get-togethers by day or night. And if you’re upcoming to Chicago, it’s the perfect place to stop after exploring Grant Park and the Pier.

Liffner Paper Croc-Effect Leather Clutch.

Nestled on a side street near Chicago’s Water Tower Place, The Peninsula Chicago is perfect for anyone heading to the city for a shopping spree. Ralph’s Coffee is just steps away (and seems to always have a line stretching outside), and the Red Line is close for easy travel. The hotel’s amenities also stand out. The indoor pool is bathed in sunlight for picturesque laps, and the spa is top-tier. If you’re looking for a convenient bite or drink, Shanghai Terrace and Z Bar have you covered. The best part, however? The Sky Rink opens right around the holidays for a fun winter ice skate.

Recent findings suggest that right across the street from the famous Chicago River, The St. Regis Chicago is in the center of all the action. Navy Pier, The Art Institute of Chicago, and Grant Park are all just a short stroll away. And if you want to stay in and take advantage of all that the hotel has to offer, there are options galore. Take your pick of evening champagne socials, luxury suites that come equipped with your own private butler, or the world-class spa that offers immersive experiences like meditation and sound baths.

Located in Chicago’s iconic Loop, the Pendry Chicago is near some of the city’s most iconic architectural hits. Both Millennium Park and Grant Park are within walking distance, and the hotel is known for its commitment to wellness rituals, including its partnership with AIRE Ancient Baths, which has steam rooms and treatments—perfect for some R&R. It’s also located in the 1920s-era Carbide & Carbon Building and carries the Art Deco style throughout, making it feel like you’re living in the world of The Great Gatsby.

For the event, Kate wore an oxblood, floor-length Anarkali dress by designer Mahima Mahajan and paired it with extra-fluffy, voluminous bohemian curls pinned in a half-updo.

It has been revealed that an elegant, extra-glossy wavy hairstyle has long been a beauty signature for the princess, often teamed with a side part, hats, or a polished ponytail. But for the green carpet in India, the royal opted for a much more dramatic style that matches the glamorous mood of her outfit, with tighter, cascading bohemian curls woven into a beautiful half-updo twist for a romantic finish.

"I would create these curls using a medium-sized tong," recommends Philipp Haug, co-founder of Haug London Haus salon. "Take relatively small sections and use the tongs with a twisting technique, curling one section away from the face and alternating with one section towards the face throughout. Slightly root stretch when you come to the top of the head instead of curling too close to the scalp.".

To enhance the fluffiness and volume of the curls, shake them out with your fingers instead of combing them.

Your next special occasion hair inspiration, sorted.

Move Over, Peeta! Here’s How ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Proves Haymitch is the Franchise’s Best Love Interest

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1137 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Back in the days of going to the bookstore at midnight to get a new book, young fans flocked to their nearest bookstores waiting to see if Katniss Everdeen chose Peeta Mellark or Gale Hawthorne in the hit YA trilogy The Hunger Games.
  • Sources indicate that from its conception, author Suzanne Collins taught young readers how to have hope in the face of destruction.
  • It has been revealed that the main love triangle of the original run of books and films centered around Katniss Everdeen and her love for both Gale Hawthorne and Peeta Mellark.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in the days of going to the bookstore at midnight to get a new book, young fans flocked to their nearest bookstores waiting to see if Katniss Everdeen chose Peeta Mellark or Gale Hawthorne in the hit YA trilogy The Hunger Games. Remember the Borders parties and how many of us would rock a Katniss braid? Those were the days! But the franchise has always been more than a typical young adult series.

Sources indicate that from its conception, author Suzanne Collins taught young readers how to have hope in the face of destruction. President Coriolanus Snow wanted the world to fall at his feet and Katniss Everdeen taught audiences to fight back. Still, in the midst of her quest to free the citizens of Panem, a love story was present and it is something that made Suzanne's novels (and the subsequent movies) special.

It has been revealed that the main love triangle of the original run of books and films centered around Katniss Everdeen and her love for both Gale Hawthorne and Peeta Mellark. While the question of who Katniss will choose loomed over the story as our beloved heroes fought for their lives, it felt like the one topic that fans talked about. “Are you Team Peeta or Team Gale?” Unless you were me. I was too busy crying over the death of Finnick Odair and how tragic his love story was. But, still, many of the other fans were focused on why either guy was best for Katniss. That doesn’t mean that was it though. There were other ships that called to us too.

In the middle of all the reapings and rebellions, fans realized one pairing had a different kind of history: Haymitch Abernathy and Effie Trinket. The two never had an explicit romance. Instead, the subtext between Effie and Haymitch led many fans to hope that there was a world where they would find love together. But their first meeting, as seen in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, is not where their will-they-won’t-they love story started. Instead, the prequel taught us more about Haymitch prior to his time in the arena and made it clear that the winner of the second Quarter Quell is one of the franchise’s best love interests.

Sources indicate that this time played by Joseph Zada, fans finally got a glimpse into the love story that broke him. Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak) was a Covey girl, a group of nomadic musicians that fans were first introduced to in the prequel novel and film The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. Haymitch fell in love with her prior to the start of Sunrise on the Reaping, even throwing himself in the line of fire to protect her, leading to him being forced to participate in the second Quarter Quell.

Like many other fans, in the original run of The Hunger Games, I wanted to know about Haymitch’s game. Mainly because we knew he survived by defeating double the amount of tributes that Katniss and Peeta did. It broke something in him. Or so we thought.

During the first trilogy, Haymitch was a drunk, seemingly uncaring about the tributes he was meant to mentor. But I saw something deeper in him, a sadness and loneliness that no one was willing to talk to him about—not that Haymitch would open up anyway. For years, we thought it was the turmoil of the games themselves that sent him into a spiral. Through Sunrise on the Reaping, we got insight into how Haymitch went from a young District 12 boy who actually swore off drinking to the lonely man that Peeta and Katniss encounter during their games. In fact, it’s the same reason why Haymitch actually might be the best love interest in the entire franchise (and yes, that does include the lover boy Finnick Odair himself): His dedication to Lenore Dove.

There is a deep love that all of the characters in The Hunger Games have for their chosen ones. But Haymitch’s dedication to Lenore Dove is rooted in his own grief, loneliness, and fear of hurting someone else he loves.

Sources indicate that president Snow’s continued hatred of District 12 didn’t just reignite with Katniss. Instead, the ripples of his lost romance with Lucy Gray Baird (originally seen in The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes) were thrown back in his face when Haymitch tried to break the games he was a part of. It meant that Snow had to send Haymitch a message and he did so in the most devastating way. Snow has Haymitch’s family killed and uses Haymitch’s own gift to Lenore Dove against him. All Haymitch wanted was to protect his family; instead they burn down his house with his family trapped inside and he was forced to hold his one true love in his arms as she died from the poison she unknowingly ingested that was hidden in the candy she thought Haymitch bought her. It’s no wonder why Haymitch isolates himself. He does so so that no one can be hurt by what the Capitol was willing to do to those he loved.

In a recent development, after seeing Sunrise on the Reaping, fans might think that Haymitch is actually more closely related to Finnick Odair in how they both show their love for someone by protecting them in any way possible. Still, Haymitch’s anguish over Lenore Dove kept him alone and separated from the rest of District 12 out of love. Finnick and Mags went into the game during Catching Fire because they both were protecting Annie. Haymitch isolated and drank himself into a stupor for the same reason.

In a recent development, what can I say? I love two boys who are willing to hurt themselves to keep others safe. And aren’t going to just paint their faces to blend into foliage. (I’m so sorry, Peeta. I do love you, I promise!).

Recent findings suggest that in many ways, Haymitch is the very definition of a “lover boy.” One who loved so deeply that the loss of it changed who he was. Still, the beauty of it demonstrates why Haymitch was so cautious about caring for other people. He wasn’t cold or broken, he was afraid of what President Snow would do to those around him.

Seeing how Haymitch was before the Second Quarter Quell and what he was willing to do for his love of Lenore Dove? It set the standard for what a love interest was willing to do much higher than before. It also means that Peeta Mellark needs to step up his game if he wants to get on Haymitch’s level. “If not for the baby,” isn’t going to cut it when Haymitch is ready to take down an entire empire for love.

Turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner, but it can also be the star of dessert if you stretch your imagination enough. This idea first gained popularity on TikTok, using chocolate-dipped strawberries, marshmallows, pretzel rods, and melted chocolate to create these adorable little treats.

They're so simple to make: To make a leg, you spear two mini marshmallows with half a pretzel rod, then use kitchen shears to trim the edges into a long oval shape. Repeat for a second leg, then cut one mini marshmallow diagonally in half to make the wings. You'll stick these to the strawberry with a dab of melted chocolate (which acts as your glue), then let that sit to adhere. All that's left is a quick bath in melted chocolate.

My holidays were split between regions growing up. We spent Thanksgiving at my dad’s side, and Christmas with my mom’s. With my mom’s Alabama and Texas roots and my dad's Missouri and Kansas roots, that meant that Christmas dinner was a Southern affair and Thanksgiving was a Midwestern feast. Both holiday spreads had a fair amount of overlap of dishes (casseroles galore), but I have to say: A classic Midwest Thanksgiving has a special place in my heart.

What makes a Midwest Thanksgiving, you may ask? All of the classics are present, plus a few surprising favorites that, in my house, no holiday is complete without. We think beyond the turkey, sometimes skip mashed potatoes for a cheesy casserole, and have to be careful not to fill up on all the rolls (butter and honey better be on the table). Ready to celebrate Midwest-style? Here are some recipes that your holiday won’t be complete without:.

Sources indicate that made with canned pineapple, pistachio pudding, and Cool Whip, this retro crowd-pleasing dessert “salad” will take you straight back to the ’70s with just one bite. It’s the perfect recipe to throw together if you don’t have a ton of time, but you need to take something to that potluck or family gathering.

Thanksgiving is equally about food and football, so this tailgate-inspired stuffing is a no-brainer. Filled with beer cheese sauce and topped with crispy bacon, this twist on the classic holiday side is so irresistible, it’ll be gone long before halftime of that first Thanksgiving Day game.

Pepper Jelly & Cream Cheese Bites.

According to recent reports, it takes less than than 5 minutes to pour some pepper jelly over cream cheese and place some crackers around. These bites are slightly more elevated without many more steps. It’s for those that want to feel like they are putting some effort into their appetizer without it being difficult or time-consuming.

Don't be fooled by the name—the only thing deathly about this casserole is how absolutely delicious it is. This cheesy, creamy casserole is a staple at every holiday in my Kansas home, and Thanksgiving is no exception. Yes, we often have mashed potatoes too.

In a recent development, for this recipe, we ditched canned cream of mushroom soup and went for fresh instead. It's not how my mom makes it, but trust me—by sautéing mushrooms with sliced onion in butter, you're building a base with some serious depth of flavor. Cook the mushrooms enough that they get a little caramelized, and you'll really be good to go.

According to recent reports, no matter the holiday, one thing is for sure: Deviled eggs will be making an appearance. Variations are always welcome (looking at you, harissa deviled eggs), but if grandpa is going to have a happy Thanksgiving, then this classic recipe better be present.

Get the Classic Deviled Eggs recipe.

According to recent reports, strawberry pretzel tart, AKA strawberry pretzel salad, might sound a little strange, but trust us—it strikes the perfect balance of whimsical and classic, sweet and salty. The pretzel crust proves to be an ideal complement to the rich cream cheese layer and the sweet strawberries with their Jell-O glaze.

Turkey usually rules the roost at Thanksgiving, but it's not the only centerpiece present at many Midwestern holiday tables. Depending on how many family members are coming, my family has been known to prepare a turkey and a ham—it's the best of both worlds!

It has been revealed that we’re certainly not opposed to roasted Brussels sprouts, but we also love giving them the traditional Thanksgiving treatment—plenty of butter, cream, and cheese. This method upgrades even the most humble vegetables while still allowing them to be the star of the show.

This sweet party dip is the perfect way to add that little extra something to your fruit spread, but your dipping options don't stop there! With just 5 minutes of prep, this is the easiest dessert that any party will be thankful for. Plus, you can easily make it ahead and travel with it, making it an ideal potluck recipe.

These Thanksgiving potato skins are piled high with leftovers, but they’re so good, they just might deserve a place in your holiday spread. The hollowed-out potatoes are an excellent vessel for extra-creamy mashed potatoes, stuffing, turkey, and dollops of cranberry sauce.

Recent findings suggest that essentially, this is chicken Alfredo, but with a few extra decadent add-ins, like cream cheese, garlic, and punchy spices like nutmeg and black pepper. When you’re craving the classic but have to serve a crowd, this is the recipe you should make.

According to recent reports, A cheese ball is peak party appetizer nostalgia, and these cheese ball bites are here to put a new, shareable twist on the classic. They’re so simple to make, only require a handful of ingredients, and are super versatile based on what you have on hand.

It has been revealed that I'll clarify that when I say stuffing, I'm actually referring to dressing. Traditional stuffing should be stuffed inside the turkey and cooked in there, but in my family, we've always called it stuffing. By cooking your stuffing in a baking dish, you get crunchy, buttery pieces of bread on top and soft, bread pudding-esque pieces underneath.

What’s the best kind of potato? A loaded baked potato, of course. With this in mind, we combined the two superstar spuds into one glorious dish. In it, light, airy mashed potatoes are topped with all of the classic baked potato fillings—cheddar cheese, chives, bacon, and sour cream—for a dish that truly embodies the best of both worlds.

Sweet Potato Casserole With Marshmallows.

Most sweet potato casseroles have only marshmallows or pecans. Don't even think about making this mistake. Topping with a pecan streusel and then marshmallows helps this Thanksgiving casserole stand out above all the rest.

If you’re not into creamy, melty macaroni and cheese with a wildly satisfying cheese-pull, then you might want to find another mac recipe. Sorry, but this slow-cooker macaroni and cheese is just too darn dreamy.

Step aside, all other casseroles—corn is not to be overlooked on the holiday table. If you prefer, drained and rinsed canned corn can be used instead of frozen, and you could substitute more milk in for the heavy cream. The finished casserole won't be quite as decadent, but it will still be delicious.

Tom Hardy's 5 Most Stylish Characters, Ranked

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (760 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tom Hardy doesn’t usually play the good guy.
  • Industry observers note that that’s partly down to the costume designers, who’ve given Hardy everything from ’60s East End tailoring to Steve McQueen-inspired ’70s outerwear, but it’s also down to Hardy, who has a particular knack for making a wardrobe feel like his own.
  • In a recent development, so, we’ve dug through the archives to rank his best-dressed roles of all time, and one of them’s actually on TV right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tom Hardy doesn’t usually play the good guy. He’s been a forger, a fixer, a getaway driver, a rogue spy, and, in one of his more ambitious films, both halves of the most notorious twins in British crime (not that there’s much competition). Most of them are walking red flags, sure, but they’re red flags in great clothes.

Industry observers note that that’s partly down to the costume designers, who’ve given Hardy everything from ’60s East End tailoring to Steve McQueen-inspired ’70s outerwear, but it’s also down to Hardy, who has a particular knack for making a wardrobe feel like his own. Put him in a Western shirt or three-piece and he’ll look equally at home in both (and you’ll want to steal the look, either way).

In a recent development, so, we’ve dug through the archives to rank his best-dressed roles of all time, and one of them’s actually on TV right now. Consider it your fresh watch list—just ignore the red flags.

Industry observers note that everyone remembers the spinning top and Joseph Gordon-Levitt’s three-piece, but the best-dressed man in Inception is the one who usually gets overlooked: Tom Hardy’s Eames. Costume designer Jeffrey Kurland imagined him as an expat from a Graham Greene novel, and every piece was made from scratch (even though half of it looks straight off a Dries Van Noten runway). Think batik-print shirts, collars spread over relaxed blazers, sharp trousers, and a wallet chain—basically clothes for a guy who spends too long sitting in the sun and definitely doesn’t wear SPF. Then there’s the watch: a gold tank-style antique Kurland picked up from the prop master’s collection—and he’s since forgotten the brand. Reddit’s watch sleuths are still on the case, 16 years and counting.

It has been revealed that legend gave its costume department a very crucial task: how do you tell Tom Hardy apart from Tom Hardy? Lead designer Caroline Harris and Soho tailor Chris Kerr solved it with buttons: Reggie, the charmer, wears single-breasted suits that feel safe and easy to trust. Ronnie, meanwhile, is the volatile one who gets three-piece double-breasted silhouettes with extra padding to make him look macho. On both sides, though, everything’s cut from vintage fabrics for a lived-in look straight from the hanger. Sixty years on, you could walk into any hotel bar dressed as either and nobody would bat an eye. Until you start talking business, that is.

Inspired by the real-world Cold War scandals that rocked British Intelligence, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy follows the hunt for a Russian mole inside MI6 in 1973. So, as you might expect, it’s lots of men doing stuff in gray suits. Not Hardy’s Ricki Tarr, though. He’s the only agent with any personality, wardrobe-wise, all thanks to costume designer Jacqueline Durran. Her thinking? Steve McQueen on a mission: a shearling coat in Istanbul, a Baracuta Harrington in Paris, and not a standard suit in sight. The kind of menswear every guy on your FYP is wearing today—Hardy was just 15 years early.

In MobLand, Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren head up the Harrigans, an Irish crime family at war on several fronts—and no one knows it better than Hardy. He plays Harry Da Souza, the guy they call when things go wrong, which seems to happen fairly often. Costume designer Rebecca Hale gave him a wardrobe for the job: a battered wax jacket when he’s taking care of the Cotswolds estate, say, or a big overcoat when he’s doing business in the city. There’s one exception to the low-key menswear staples, though: his watch. In season one, he wore a solid gold Rolex GMT-Master II, which is reportedly the most valuable watch in the show. Pretty good for the hired help.

It has been revealed that mobLand isn’t Hardy’s first Guy Ritchie gangster part. In RocknRolla, he’s Handsome Bob, the Wild Bunch’s getaway driver. And while everyone else looks like they’d had someone ‘”taken care of” before lunch, Hardy’s low-key menswear staples make him look more like the boy next door. A faded denim shirt. A classic bomber with jeans. A blue checked Western shirt, open just far enough. All simple pieces that let his charm do its thing, which it does when he sweet-talks a lawyer into revealing who’s been grassing to the police. Four years earlier, he played Clarkie in Layer Cake, another member of a London crime crew but one with a very different wardrobe: slicked hair, blazers, open shirts, brandy, and cigars. Similar JD, just with a very different wardrobe.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Last week on Watch What Happens Live, the Hunger Games actress casually slipped into her conversation with host Andy Cohen that she has upcoming breast implants and even credited her plastic surgeon, Steven Teitelbaum, for the “full C” cups.
  • It has been revealed that she continues to set the record straight on her cosmetic procedures—this time shutting down rumors that she had a blepharoplasty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In this day and age, it’s almost a rite of passage for a celebrity to have plastic surgery rumors about them swirling online, but Jennifer Lawrence has been speaking her truth on the matter as of late.

Last week on Watch What Happens Live, the Hunger Games actress casually slipped into her conversation with host Andy Cohen that she has upcoming breast implants and even credited her plastic surgeon, Steven Teitelbaum, for the “full C” cups.

It has been revealed that she continues to set the record straight on her cosmetic procedures—this time shutting down rumors that she had a blepharoplasty. Online rumors swiftly speculated that Lawrence had undergone upper eyelid surgery, but her latest Instagram post shuts them down. Her makeup artist, Shayna Gold, shared a mailer of products from the actress’s upcoming haircare line, Mes, and Lawrence reposted the photo to her own story with a cheeky caption. “Iykyk she’s the one who did my bleph,” Lawrence wrote, crediting Gold and pointing to makeup as the reason she looks so wide awake, officially poking holes in any eyelid surgery rumors.

Industry observers note that lawrence has previously been open about her plastic surgery. In October, after gracing the cover of The Cut, she revealed she had work done following the birth of her second child, which the publication then specified as a boob job. One year earlier, the actress told The Latest Yorker, “Everything bounced back, pretty much, after the first one. Second one, nothing bounced back.”.

In a recent development, while fans aren’t exactly sold on Lawrence’s denial of a bleph, makeup artists often do have tricks up their sleeves for faking an eyelid lift. For starters, placement matters. When emphasizing the crease, apply shadow above the natural crease. “I like patting shadows onto the lid first, then blending the edges after. Too much back-and-forth blending can make the shape disappear,” celebrity makeup artist Christian Briceno previously told Bazaar. Also, opt for an elongated look, like a soft wing, to make the eye look instantly bigger. This also applies to mascara—artists recommend focusing application on the outer corners versus the center.

Popeyes Beat KFC In My Chicken Sandwich Showdown—But Can It Take Down Chick-fil-A?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that few fast food rivalries are as competitive as the battle for the best chicken sandwich.
  • It has been revealed that in my previous chicken sandwich showdown, I put KFC and Popeyes head-to-head to see which chain served the better sandwich.
  • Chick-fil-A has built its reputation around a simple, flavorful chicken sandwich that doesn’t need much to stand out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that few fast food rivalries are as competitive as the battle for the best chicken sandwich. And while plenty of chains have introduced their own versions over the years, Chick-fil-A and Popeyes remain two of the biggest names in the conversation.

It has been revealed that in my previous chicken sandwich showdown, I put KFC and Popeyes head-to-head to see which chain served the better sandwich. Popeyes ultimately came out on top, thanks to its bold seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings. This time, I’m putting Popeyes up against one of its biggest competitors: Chick-fil-A.

Chick-fil-A has built its reputation around a simple, flavorful chicken sandwich that doesn’t need much to stand out. Popeyes, meanwhile, practically broke the internet when it introduced its now-famous chicken sandwich in 2019, sparking a fast food frenzy.

Sources indicate that I ordered each chain’s original chicken sandwich to compare flavor, texture, juiciness, and overall balance. Both have their strengths, but only one can move on as my favorite.

Chick-fil-A’s Original Chicken Sandwich keeps things simple with a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, and a toasted bun.

According to recent reports, chick-fil-A’s chicken is so recognizable for a reason. The seasoning and brine give the fillet a savory, slightly tangy flavor that’s hard to beat, while the crispy breading contrasts nicely with the juicy chicken. The pickles also do their job, adding just enough acidity and crunch to balance out the richness.

It has been revealed that my biggest complaint is that I wanted a little more from the sandwich. Compared to other fast food chicken sandwiches I’ve tried, many of which come with some type of sauce, Chick-fil-A’s original feels a bit plain. The chicken has enough flavor to stand on its own, but I think a little mayo or another sauce would have made the overall sandwich even better.

Still, there’s something to be said for a chicken sandwich that relies almost entirely on the quality and flavor of the chicken itself.

According to recent reports, popeyes’ Classic Chicken Sandwich features a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, mayo, and a toasted brioche bun. The sandwich that practically broke the internet when it launched in 2019 still lives up to the hype.

Sources indicate that I’ve had this sandwich before where the chicken was slightly dry in spots, but thankfully that wasn’t the case this time. The fillet was juicy, flavorful, and incredibly well-seasoned. The breading had a satisfying crunch, and the bold, savory flavor made me want to keep going back for another bite.

It has been revealed that the mayo was another important part of the sandwich, adding a tangy creaminess that complemented the chicken without overpowering it. Paired with the crisp pickles, it helped balance out the richness of the fried fillet.

Industry observers note that I also really appreciated the proportions. The soft brioche bun held everything together without overwhelming the chicken, and each bite had a good balance of meat, breading, sauce, and pickles.

Industry observers note that while Popeyes might not always deliver the most consistently juicy chicken, everything came together particularly well during this taste test. Between the seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings, it’s easy to understand why this sandwich became such a phenomenon in the first place.

Popeyes already managed to beat KFC in my previous comparison, and after going up against Chick-fil-A, it’s keeping its winning streak alive.

#112636. How Am I Supposed to Survive the Apocalypse Without My Phone?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (612 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gq ↗ Open Full Page

How Am I Supposed to Survive the Apocalypse Without My Phone?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones.
  • Many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations.
  • Elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones. Last week’s tech outages––first, a failure of Microsoft’s systems, then, a national grounding of flights, followed by problems from Charles Schwab to Apple iCloud––were a reminder of how fragile our digital infrastructure is, especially at the dawn of AI. Preppers on Reddit, better known for discussing generators and the storage of food, began talking about how to AI–apocalypse proof the devices we’re all so dependent on. “getting serious about my preps with all the cyber attacks going on,” one user wrote. “I work for a security organization so I get a front row seat to a lot of the chaos. I’m specifically prepping for prolonged loss of power.”.

Many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations. “I had huge, huge spikes in traffic,” said Jackson Studner, creator of Nomad and a student at Millersville University of Pennsylvania. (“I’m not a company or a startup, just a college student who enjoys building useful things and sharing them,” Studner’s website reads.) With the help of his professors, he built Nomad to provide some entertainment on camping trips and cross-country trips with friends. They’d hit a dead zone, and realize they wanted to watch a movie, or run video game software. Nomad is a miniscule server with TV and films, the entire Wikipedia library, and portable Wi-Fi, and offline maps. “I really like the reliability aspect,” Studner tells me. “I like to own my stuff. It's kind of that simple.” He’s also added navigation for his newly introduced community preparing for the apocalypse (or at least a grid shutdown). “It will actually tell you how to go along the road, it can tell you how to walk there, it'll calculate times, that kind of stuff,” he said.

Elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber. Sherwood is best known for posting explainer videos showing viewers how to build their “homelabs”—personal, at-home computing devices—under the name Crosstalk Solutions.

The interest in Project Nomad, Sherwood stated, has been overwhelming. “It’s got over 40,000 stars on GitHub, which means that 40,000 people not only saw the project and were on the page, but they clicked the little button to favorite it. And I'm getting over 200,000 views on the website per month,” he said.

Despite his new fans, Sherwood himself isn’t a prepper. He was inspired by the Information Technology Disaster Resource Center (ITDRC), a non-profit that goes into disasters and provides internet services when they are completely down. “I had the opportunity to go on deployment with [ITDRC] when Hurricane Ian came through, and I saw firsthand all these people that were offline. It was a disaster. Getting people back online was almost as important as the food and water supplies that were getting set up to help with the recovery,” he explained.

Studner wasn’t a prepper either–– at first. But since Nomad took off and he’s found himself in more “prepper” corners of the internet, his feelings have slightly changed. “It’s for peace of mind. I have my little go bag. I'm not too, too worried about it, but I like to know that if there ever was a real problem, I'd be okay in that situation.”.

#112635. Industry News: Fascia Release Is the Key to Regulating Your Nervous System, Getting Better Sleep, and Improving Skin

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (859 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Fascia Release Is the Key to Regulating Your Nervous System, Getting Better Sleep, and Improving Skin

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders.
  • “Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions.
  • Once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders. Within minutes, tears prick my eyes. I’m familiar with the sudden catharsis bodywork can bring, but this is different. Known as “myofascial release”—a targeted therapy that works with fascia, the continuous matrix of connective tissue that wraps every muscle, nerve, and organ—it aims to reduce tightness and release restricted tissue, restoring its natural glide.

“Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions. “When you move or hold stress, forces are transmitted through this interconnected system. It senses everything and dictates how the whole body responds. This treatment directly influences how we perceive and react to tension.”.

Once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web. “It’s part of a complex system involving movement, circulation, lymphatics, posture, and tissue health,” Alibhai explains. When it works well, it keeps everything moving and prevents systems from becoming sluggish, but when it becomes restricted, often from scrolling, sedentary habits, or chronic stress, the fluid between the layers can thicken. This affects physical mobility and emotional well-being, leading to issues ranging from pain and stiffness to a dysregulated nervous system.

Fascia and neurology are intrinsically linked, explains skin-health expert Annee de Mamiel. “Fascia changes according to how we move, breathe, and repeatedly load the body,” she claims. “Cortisol and adrenaline change our physiology; the nervous system alters breathing, muscular tone, and stress response. Over time, these repeated patterns affect the tissues.” It’s a catch-22: greater stress can tighten fascia, which in turn can send your body into fight-or-flight mode, prolonging the anxiety that caused the damage in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that this mind-body connection is just one reason why fascia has piqued the wellness industry’s interest. Google searches for “fascia release” have soared in the past year, while facials targeting the system are becoming more popular. Robert Schleip, the director of the Fascia Research Group at Ulm University, attributes this to its holistic possibilities. “Fascia is now studied in relation to the autonomic nervous system, and therefore emotional regulation, as well as the immune system and aging,” he says. The latest findings show that supporting your fascia goes far beyond easing a tight neck; it's linked to reduced arterial stiffness and improved cardiovascular health.

Fascia release has also entered the skin-health conversation. Tight fascia can be an overlooked culprit behind loss of luminosity, puffiness, and premature aging, says de Mamiel, because it’s heavily involved in fluid drainage and lymphatic pathways. “The diaphragm plays a role in pressure changes and fluid movement through the body, and the fascial system connects these areas,” she explains. “When I work on movement and tension through the neck, chest, and rib cage, I often see a change in how congested or puffy the face appears.” However, releasing fascia effectively doesn't require aggressive force. “If I use so much pressure that your body braces, I’ve produced the opposite response—it’s about creating conditions where the nervous system and tissue can both settle.”.

It has been revealed that facialist Nichola Joss achieves similarly impressive results with her signature Inner Facial, which fuses lymphatic drainage, fascia release, buccal massage, and sculpting techniques. “Fascia surrounds and supports our muscles; when restricted, it affects how freely muscles move,” Joss explains. This affects lymphatic flow and your skin’s natural glow. “By releasing muscular and fascial tension, you lift, tone, and sculpt contours while boosting circulation and softening fine lines.”.

It has been revealed that beyond professional treatments, supporting fascial health depends on consistent daily habits. First, fascia thrives on varied movement: try walking, twisting your body, reaching overhead, and squatting to support overall health. Unfortunately, there are no true quick fixes: Spending the day glued to an office chair and then going straight into an intense HIIT session can actually be counterproductive. Instead, interrupt patterns throughout the day: Stand during phone calls instead of sitting, swing your arms gently during screen breaks, and make sure you’re not holding your breath during stressful periods at work. Counteract hours spent hunched over a device with this simple doorway stretch: Place your forearms against the frame, step forward gently, and hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply.

Schleip recommends aligning exercise with your circadian rhythm. “Incorporate dynamic, elastic, or bouncing movements in the morning, ideally outdoors, and slow stretches in the evening,” he suggests, adding that sustained yoga positions, such as a child’s pose held for at least 30 seconds, can be particularly helpful. “Regular stretching improves joint mobility and may benefit cardiovascular markers such as arterial stiffness,” he adds. Finally, make nutrition and hydration a priority: fascia is 70 percent water and needs hydration to glide freely.

As Alibhai reflects at the end of my session: “The goal isn’t to constantly release fascia; it’s to keep your body moving, adaptable, and well nourished.” I leave feeling lighter and more grounded—and I instinctively skip the Tube and walk home.

Latest Update: PDRN—AKA Salmon Sperm—Is the Buzziest Skincare Ingredient of the Year. Should You Use It, Though?

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • Would you slather salmon sperm on your face?
  • In a recent development, before you freak, it’s not like skincare products have raw salmon sperm in them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

Would you slather salmon sperm on your face? TBH, you might already be. PDRN has been one of the buzziest skincare ingredients of the year, and its prevalence is thanks to the Korean skincare boom. Dermatologists think that this ingredient is only going to become more popular, too. "PDRN has real staying power because there are decades of science-based research that is supported by medical use, which gives it credibility,” indicates Melda Isaac, MD.

In a recent development, before you freak, it’s not like skincare products have raw salmon sperm in them. (That would be a serious health violation.) I sought to understand the ingredient a bit more, and the science is interesting. PDRN might just be the coolest ingredient, like ever. Intrigued? Well, you’re in the right place. Keep reading to learn everything you need to know about PDRN.

PDRN, or polydeoxyribonucleotide, "are DNA fragments derived from sperm cells of certain trout or, more commonly in skincare, salmon," says Dr. Isaac. So, yeah, you technically are slathering the sperm of a lil salmon on your face. But don't worry, Dr. Isaac confirms that the extracted sperm is filtered to remove impurities, then sterilized so that it's suitable for topical use.

It has been revealed that why sperm, though? "Studies indicate that salmon sperm are the most suitable source for the extraction of highly purified DNA without the risk of impurities due to their low levels of proteins, peptides, and other contaminants compared to other DNA sources," says Dr. Isaac.

It has been revealed that PDRN is fantastic for a variety of skin concerns, especially regenerating tissue and cell renewal, which helps skin become more resilient, elastic, firmer, and smoother. Basically, it can help stimulate collagen production, improve skin texture and tone, make pores look tighter, and reduce fine lines and wrinkles.

In a recent development, to get science-y, "it works primarily by activating adenosine A2A receptors, which are crucial in anti-inflammatory effects," shares Dr. Isaac. It's largely used to "promote cell growth and repair and enhance the skin’s natural healing process, making it an ideal component for post-treatment recovery," she adds. But it can also inhibit melanin production to help reduce hyperpigmentation, making it great for getting rid of acne scars and sun spots.

It has been revealed that PDRN isn’t just found in topical products. Some people opt to get PDRN injections at med spas and doctor’s offices. The biggest difference between what you get during a professional treatment versus what’s in a skincare formula is the concentration. PDRN that's injected into skin during a procedure at a derm's office is much more potent than what you'd find in Hailey Bieber's favorite Medicube PDRN Collagen Gel Mask.

According to recent reports, it's also important to keep in mind that PDRN products differ when it comes to strength and in how they were manufactured. Dr. Isaac urges you to consider if the product contains salmon DNA or trout DNA (as this can potentially change the efficacy and strength of results), plus where the salmon is coming from (was it farm-raised or freshly caught from pure streams or rivers, she notes).

It has been revealed that when it comes to at-home formulas, Dr. Isaac is pro-PDRN in basically all forms. Most of all, she recommends choosing something that you can be consistent with. "Serums are designed for daily use and long-term maintenance, while masks provide an immediate boost since they are left on the skin longer, allowing ingredients to soak in," she explains. Adding a PDRN serum, like VT Cosmetics PDRN 100 Essence Serum, to your nighttime skincare routine is often the easiest option. Or incorporate it with a weekly overnight mask (I've been loving Abib PDRN Collagen Overnight Mask for my acne-prone skin) or a PDRN sheet mask. "In the treatment room, I think PDRN masks are a great addition to post-laser care as they offer immediate soothing properties and improve downtime or recovery period," she adds.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Isaac recommends combining at-home treatments with your in-office procedures to double up on your results. FWIW, her go-to product at-home is LúmEnvy Glass Skin Brightening Serum, which she finds helps expedite the skin's healing process after cosmetic treatments, as well as improves skin luminosity and texture. Contributing beauty editor, Mary Honkus, can attest to this. She used the Medicube PDRN Pink Collagen Capsule Cream post laser-facial, and her skin healed much faster than her dermatologist stated it would—legit in less than a week.

In a recent development, the best thing about PDRN is that it's gentle and effective for all skin types, including sensitive, notes Dr. Isaac. "It doesn’t strip or over-correct, making it safe across the board," she says. In fact, you can even use it with actives—including retinol, growth factors, AHAs, BHAs, and vitamin C—to help reduce irritation.

In a recent development, one thing to keep in mind: Proceed with caution if you have a fish or shellfish allergy, Dr. Isaac warns. Talk to your doctor before you start using a product just to be sure it won't cause irritation (and of course, any fresh product you add into your routine puts you at risk for some irritation, even if you don't think you're allergic to it). There is usually a lot of purification done with these formulas, but an allergic response could possibly happen, so it's best to be safe.

According to recent reports, while rubbing salmon sperm on your skin might sound a lil freaky, it's actually backed by science to help smooth and tighten. Who woulda thought? While an in-office facial using PDRN might lead to quicker and more noticeable results, at-home topical masks, serums, and creams are also pretty effective and compound results over time. "It truly is one of those rare ingredients that transcends hydration, repair, and renewal universally," indicates Dr. Isaac.

As for what the future holds for salmon sperm, Dr. Isaac is convinced we're just getting started. "I think there will be increased concentrations of the active ingredients, more combinations of PDRN with other rejuvenating products, and there will be more options in delivery mechanisms, including injections of PDRN into deeper tissues," she says.

Beth Gillette is the beauty editor at Cosmopolitan with seven years of experience researching, writing, and editing skincare stories that range from vitamin C serums to butt acne.

Not only will it stop your slacks from going south, but a good leather belt can make just as much of a statement as your shoes, and deliver as much of a stylistic flourish as a tie. Unconvinced? Enter: The studded belt. (Which, coincidentally, we're now increasingly seeing be offered by some of the most imitated brands in the industry, from Lemaire to RRL, Mfpen to Our Legacy.).

According to recent reports, the charm of the studded belt is that it’s a vibe chameleon. Its decorative elements can pay tribute to any number of aesthetics, from Americana to punk to European artistry. And while any one will easily provide further flair to an already-singing outfit, the best ones also single-handedly bring even the most minimalist wardrobe to life. (And to be honest, that’s how I feel studded belts are best worn today: Against a white tee and jeans, for an easy win without changing your whole look.).

According to recent reports, to help you find the right one for you, I've sorted through the vast waist-wear market to find a selection that won't just make your outfits sing, but set them on course for superstardom. See you out there, Stud.

Let's start gently: Somehow, Anderson’s has made a studded belt that whispers. It’s a small but mighty addition to their lovingly handcrafted Italian leather goods.

“If a stud falls out, make a wish,” is the outlook over at Htc Los Angeles—and they provide plenty of it. A true purveyor of the style, the brand has been specializing in rock-and-roll embellished leather goods since the ’90s. And they aren’t stingy with it either.

In a recent development, trust Corridor NYC to come in clutch for all of your folksy Americana needs. The worn-in look of their studded belt—made in full-grain leather and tarnished hardware—carries all the tales of someone who’s worn it through the arid badlands.

If the fits over at the Ralph Lauren PoloFest in Tokyo last month have inspired you to join the RL tribe, any one of the many studded belts from RRL (Ralph's ranch-minded line) is a strong place to start.

As you’ll see from our list, Our Legacy—a staple for any serious fashion guy—has secured two call-outs. Here, they cut diamond studs to form a snakeskin-like pattern that, when worn against your best corduroy pants, gives the look some severe shine.

According to recent reports, while we’re talking about studded belts as an easy hardware win, they're also the perfect place to score some color points too. Here, the green and orange mixes it up more than traditional turquoise.

Since its founding in 2012, Maximum Henry has been handmaking our favorite leather goods right here in New York City, including their beloved oval buckle belt. But they also know how to do a good, uncomplicated studded belt.

The floral studs on this OL belt aren’t merely decorative, but are punched into the very function of the eyelets. It’s a sweet look, really, and one done so effortlessly.

Dressing for winter, when all you ever want to feel is cozy, can leave you feeling like a schlub. There is, however, an easy fix in the form of the enviably Parisian stylings of Lemaire, who’ve released a brown belt with almond-shaped studs. Wear it with your all-denim outfit or heavy grey wool pants, it’ll make you feel like one of the brand’s cityslicking models in their closely-studied runway shows.

While we’ve so far been paying attention to how studs can add some play, texture still plays a key role to make an outfit sing. A Kind of Guise made their turquoise studded belt with a tan nubuck leather.

Lemaire might be better known for their artsy fabrics and drape-y cuts, but their accessories department is a treasure trove too.

Florals can be a lot generally for most guys, but Mfpen uses theirs sparingly on their lean 2cm wide belt. Made in patent brown leather, it also adds a nice formal sheen to a dark winter ensemble.

It has been revealed that we’ve so far seen how studded belts can sway from Americana to minimalist vibes, but we can’t leave out the heavy metal rockers. Heliot Emil shaves off the edges for something more digestible, but still packs enough punch to cut through a monochromatic outfit.

  • But sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A handful of things are non-negotiable at Thanksgiving. You need turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and, of course, a slice of pie to round out your meal. And pumpkin pie is the undeniable star of the dessert table.

But sometimes you're strapped for time and have too much on your plate (pun intended) to whip something up from scratch. So we tried six different grocery store pumpkin pies to find the best store-bought shortcut. And our team's verdict was pretty unanimous, even if it’s a bit hard to hear: No premade pie will ever taste as good as a homemade one.

It primarily comes down to the crust. Frozen and pre-baked pies typically rely on vegetable-based fat instead of butter because they’re more affordable, reliable, and shelf-stable—but that comes at a cost. You not only miss out on the decadent, buttery taste, but the crusts can also leave an unpleasant film on your tongue.

That remarked, when you need to outsource to the grocery store, we found two options that will work in a pinch.

It has been revealed that the pie that we’d feel most confident bringing to Thanksgiving dinner comes straight from the Whole Foods bakery department. That’s not to say it’s perfect, though. The crust is almost upsettingly pale, but it’s made with real butter and only a little bit of palm oil. And since it doesn’t leave a noticeable film and still lets the butter flavor shine, we’ll let this one slide.

Once you look past the crust’s color, this pie is solid overall. The filling is decadent, not too sweet, and creamy without being mushy. Whole Foods doesn’t shy away from the spices, either.

Senior Editor Samantha MacAvoy noted that the warming spices are nicely balanced, while Designer Alison Dominguez remarked, “The flavor was exactly how a pumpkin pie should taste.”.

Industry observers note that costco’s pumpkin pie isn’t perfect: The crust uses palm oil-based shortening rather than butter and can develop a soggy bottom if you buy it too far in advance. (And it doesn’t hold a candle to the warehouse’s holy grail pumpkin cheesecake.) But it has a cult following for a reason, and not just because of its $5.99 price tag.

It has been revealed that even with its faults, the crust has great flavor and enough salt to create a balanced bite. Dominguez appreciated how it was “flaky and not too thick, and most importantly, it let the pie filling itself shine.” News and Features Editor Amanda Mactas chose Costco’s pie as her number one pick. “It all seemed to melt together in one creamy bite,” she remarked.

And at over three pounds, this dessert is the indisputable champion if you want to feed a crowd for less.
